newsitem.title: USA: Nazis stole diamonds to finance war - document.
newsitem.headline: Nazis stole diamonds to finance war - document.

text.p: The Nazis used millions of dollars worth of diamonds looted from Jewish dealers in Antwerp, Belgium, to help finance their war effort, a newly released postwar document said on Monday.

A 1948 memorandum by the Belgium Mission in Germany to U.S. military authorities said that the Nazis in 1940 took control of 1,200 diamond "factories" in Antwerp and then sent their goods to Switzerland and Spain to buy foreign currency and raw materials for the war.

The memorandum, released by the World Jewish Congress, which is spearheading a search through archives to trace Nazi looting during the Second World War, said the Germans took rough diamonds worth $10 million in 1940 alone. It added that by the end of the war the cost to the Belgium economy of looted diamonds was $25 million.

The document said the Nazis set up a "Diamantkontelle" office in Antwerp that oversaw the looting and the arrest of both Jewish and non-Jewish diamond traders. Antwerp was the diamond capital of the world when the Nazis overran Belgium in 1940.

Specially authorised Nazis were then allowed to take the looted diamonds to neutral countries, mainly Switzerland and Spain, where they were used to purchase foreign currency and raw materials, the document said.
The Belgium Mission said it hoped the Americans would be able to help it recover the looted property and arrest various individuals still at large.

A man identified as Dr. Kurt Kadgien and, in one document, as the personal financial adviser to Nazi leader Hermann Goering, was described as being in charge of the Swiss end of the diamond dealing. He was said in the Belgian document to have still been in Switzerland in 1948.
